note: Presets are saved parameter sets for the same animation; they do not count as additional animations. All content is fictional and illustrative. The replacement datum and the status of the intermediate premise before and after it are supplied by the author; nothing is inferred and no conclusion is drawn.

presets.name: baseline-illustrative
presets.description: Fictional shed key: the revealed intermediate card “Whoever holds the shed key locked the shed last” (left unstated: pencil, hinges folded) is lifted out under a reading magnifier and replaced by the supplied “Only the person with the key can lock the shed”, supplied as stated: the card turns printed, both hinges latch and it lifts flush. The struck old value becomes the changed-datum tag.

presets.name: contrast-or-alternative
presets.description: Substantive alternative: a fictional library return; the CONCLUSION card is inspected and its text replaced, and the premise (stated before) is supplied as left unstated after — its hinges fold back and it drops back into its pocket.

params.facts: The blue umbrella was left at the library desk
params.rules: Items left at the desk go to lost property at closing
params.conclusion: The umbrella went to lost property
issues: Did the desk close at the usual time that day?
params.beforeValue: The umbrella went to lost property
params.afterValue: The umbrella is still waiting at the desk

contextLabels.context: Context: the library note, opened between fact and conclusion

presets.name: long-labels-stress
presets.description: Long fact, premise and conclusion texts, a long before and after value, two issues, two assumptions, long context caption and marker label.

params.facts: The only key to the garden shed was found in the inside pocket of Jo’s winter coat the next morning
params.rules: Whoever is holding the only shed key the next morning locked the shed the night before
params.conclusion: Jo is the person who locked the garden shed on the night before the key was found
issues: Who else could have opened or locked the shed that evening without the key?
Was the coat left unattended in the hall overnight?
assumptions: There is only one key and no other way to lock the shed
The coat was not lent to anyone that evening
params.beforeValue: Whoever is holding the only shed key the next morning locked the shed the night before
params.afterValue: Only a person who held the one shed key that evening could have locked the garden shed
